Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can note that I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was in Pasadena, Texas, on a two-lane road near a shopping center. It was late afternoon and traffic was
moderate.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was heading toward the intersection and slowing down for a car ahead. The other vehilce came over into my lane.
I braked, but we still met head-on, though it was a slow impact. I'd guess we were both going maybe fifteen miles an
hour.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The car lurched forward and my seatbelt locked, and my chest and lower back hit hard against the
belt.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle or go to a doctor?
A: I got out and felt okay for about an hour. By the evening my lower back was stiff and sore, and it has gotten worse
since. I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning.
Q: What did the clinic tell you?
A: They diagnosed a back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral to a physical therapist. I've been
attending sessions twice a week.
Q: Have you had any prior problems with your back?
A: I had some occasional stiffness years ago, but nothing that required treatment, and I hadn't seen anyone for it in a
long time.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sitting for long periods and lifting, and I'm cooperating fully with my treatment plan.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
